lines.text: You've seen this stack seven times. Almost everyone reads it the wrong direction.
Top to bottom, that is how it gets taught. Seven handing down to six.
But each layer has a partner. Same number, other end of the wire. That is where the message goes.
Your transport layer keeps ports and sequence numbers. So does theirs. The machines in between just forward.
Layer three is the address on the outside. Every stop reads it and sorts. Only the far end opens the letter.
Read it sideways and the stack turns into seven conversations across the wire. One layer, one partner, all at once.
Next time you see the diagram, read it sideways. All seven pairs, side by side, in the article.
